# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

# Problem

All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each SKILL.md's final-step `--ac` block replaced with concrete skill-session deliverable ACs (4 per skill for skills with multiple deliverables; 3 for simpler skills).
2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

## Skills affected

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: plan approved, children created, ACs traceable.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: keyword derivation, wl search, repo file search, summary compiled.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PERT estimate computed, risk score assessed, confidence stated, WBS suggested.
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: test failures parsed, critical items triaged, work items created/linked.
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: command spec drafted, SKILL.md written, script stub created, tests written.
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: branches assessed, stale branches pruned, orphaned stashes triaged, comments posted.
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code quality analysis run, findings documented, recommendations provided.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code smells detected, refactoring plan drafted, changes applied.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: machine pressure assessed, safe remediations proposed, actions logged.
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PR comments fetched, fixes proposed, threads resolved after approval.

## Risks

- Adding `--ac` lines to each SKILL.md is a mechanical but widespread change. Mitigation: each change is independent and reversible.
- If a skill's final-step block is very long, adding ACs + note might make it verbose. Mitigation: ACs are concise (40–60 chars each).

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling, in_review).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.

# Problem

The 4 operational/delivery skills (test, ship, implement, audit) use placeholder `--ac` values. For test/ship the session ACs are the operational deliverables (suite run, failures triaged / release promoted, audit performed). For implement/audit, the semantics are different — these skills evaluate the work item's ACs as part of their session, which is a legitimate use of `--ac`. This child clarifies the distinction and aligns with SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **test** (`skill/test/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: full test suite executed, failures parsed into triage records, critical failures triaged into work items, report rendered.
2. **ship** (`skill/ship/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: dev-to-main merge performed, audit comment posted, operator notified, CHANGELOG updated.
3. **implement** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: worktree created, tests written/updated, build green, tests green, commit made, push to dev. **Note added:** "For implement, the work-item feature ACs are evaluated during execution but are not passed to `render_report` — the report records the implement session's own success criteria. Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
4. **audit** (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: work item assessed, audit verdict determined, Ready to close line added. **Note added:** "For audit, the verdict reflects the work item's state; the report records the audit session's own success criteria (audit was performed). Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
5. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
6. Full test suite green.

## Skills affected

- `skill/test/SKILL.md`
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`

## Risks

- **Implement/audit semantics**: these skills legitimately evaluate work-item ACs. The note clarifies that the report's `--ac` table still records session success (not work-item status), and work-item ACs go in the Use Cases section.
- If SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR ("Use Cases" section) is not yet implemented, the notes reference it as a dependency.

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.

# Problem

There is no automated guard against future regressions of the placeholder-`--ac` pattern. Agents adding new report-rendering skills (or editing existing ones) might again use `--ac "<AC# description>|…|met"` placeholders instead of concrete skill-session deliverables.

SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S already added `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` which checks that every work-item skill has the final-step section and invokes `render_report`. This child extends it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` with a new test class `TestReportACConcreteness`:
   - `test_all_final_step_acs_are_concrete`: asserts each work-item skill's `--ac` lines contain at least one literal `|met` value (no placeholders like `<AC# description>`).
   - `test_all_final_steps_have_semantics_note`: asserts each work-item skill's final-step block contains a note distinguishing skill-session ACs from work-item feature ACs (search for patterns like "skill session" or "own deliverable" in the final-step block).
2. Add the new test class to the existing test file (no new test files).
3. All 6 existing hygiene tests still pass.
4. Full test suite green.

## Tests

- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — extended with `TestReportACConcreteness` (2 new tests).

## Skills covered

The test covers all 15 skills in `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` (audit, author-command, cleanup, code-review, effort-and-risk, find-related, implement, intake, machine-hygiene, plan, refactor, resolve-pr-comments, ship, test, triage).

# Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

**Headline:** The ship release close step trusts `wl close`'s exit code and reports "All N work item(s) closed successfully" even when some closes were lost by the concurrent-`wl sync` race. It must re-read persisted state, retry once, and report unclosed items by id instead of claiming blanket success.

## Problem statement

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` closes each release candidate with `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` and treats a zero exit code as success, never re-reading the item to confirm the persisted `status`/`stage`. A lost close (the `wl` lost-update race, WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) is therefore reported as a successful release — the operator only discovers dangling `in_review` work items after the fact.

## Users

- **Release operator / producer** running `/skill:ship release` — needs an accurate post-release close count so released work items are truly terminal.
- **Ship agent** executing the release pipeline — needs a verifiable close step so its summary and return value reflect reality.

Example user stories:

- As a release operator, I want the ship skill to report the true number of work items actually closed, so that I do not discover dangling `in_review` items after the release.
- As a ship agent, I want a close that exits 0 but did not persist `completed`/`done` retried once and, if still unpersisted, reported explicitly by id, so that lost closes are never silently counted as successes.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` (`run-release.js`) builds the `closable` set (after producer-review overrides, cascade, and out-of-scope refusals), then loops calling the injected `runCloseCommand(item.id, reason)`; a non-throwing call increments `closedCount`.
- On zero errors it prints and returns `All ${closedCount} work item(s) closed successfully.` — no re-read of persisted state.
- The read boundary already exists in the codebase: `getItemLifecycleFn` / `getItemLifecycle` (from `check-final-validation.js`) returns `{id, status, stage}` and is already injected for descendant terminal-state checks.
- Demonstrated failure: ToneForge v0.1.2 release (2026-10-06) reported 53/53 closed but only 50 became `completed`/`done`; three items remained `completed`/`in_review` with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt` (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18, TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8, TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G).

## Desired change

After each `runCloseCommand()` call (and once more after a bounded retry), read the item's persisted lifecycle and only count it as closed when `status === "completed"` **and** `stage === "done"`. Concretely:

1. Inject a verification read boundary (reuse `getItemLifecycleFn`, or add a dedicated `getCloseStateFn`/`verifyClosedFn` defaulting to `getItemLifecycle`).
2. Count and report `unclosedCount` / `unclosedItems` (`[{id, title, reason?}]`); never include unclosed items in `closedCount` and never emit a blanket "all closed successfully" when any attempted close did not persist.
3. Retry each unverified close **once** (bounded), re-verify, then report unclosed if still not terminal.
4. Keep the step non-blocking (failures are reported, not fatal) and preserve existing override, cascade, refusal, and `--dry-run` behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` verifies persisted state via an injectable read boundary for each attempted close instead of trusting only the close command's exit code.
2. An item that exits 0 but is not `completed`/`done` is counted as unclosed and listed by id; the summary and return value reflect it and never claim blanket success.
3. A transient lost close is retried at least once before being reported unclosed.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn` / `runCloseCommand` / verification boundary cover: (a) all closes persist → success; (b) one close is a no-op (exit 0, state unchanged) → retried, then reported unclosed; (c) retry re-persists → reported closed.
5. `npm run build` and the existing ship suites pass (no `wl` mutation from unit tests).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `skill/ship/SKILL.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test isolation (SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS):** unit tests must inject fakes; the verification boundary must be injectable and never hit the live worklog from the suite.
- **Non-blocking step:** unclosed items must not fail the release exit code (consistent with the existing close step); the fix changes reporting/return-value accuracy, not release gating.
- **Bounded retry:** at least one retry, no unbounded loop.
- **Terminal definition:** `status === "completed"` and `stage === "done"`.
- **Fail-safe on unreadable state:** if the verification read throws or returns `null`, treat the item as unverified/unclosed (never count it closed).
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** producer-review overrides, descendant cascade, out-of-scope refusals, and `--dry-run` (no mutation) must be unaffected.
- Root-cause fix of the `wl` race is out of scope (tracked on the ContextHub side).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()`: add injectable post-close verification, bounded retry, and `unclosedCount` / `unclosedItems` in the summary and return value; update the JSDoc `@returns` contract.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — add regression tests for all-persist success, no-op-then-unclosed (retried), and retry-repersists cases using injected boundaries.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the verify-and-retry close behaviour and the new unclosed reporting (Step 12 close work items).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — existing `getItemLifecycle` read boundary reused for verification (no functional change expected).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** (ContextHub) — root-cause fix: lock `wl close` against the lost-update race; child of WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7. Out of scope here; this item adds detection/visibility.
- **SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ** — the raw race report refiled to ContextHub.
- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** — ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done` (fixed by SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9 / SA-0MUTYRYEM000EEF7).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for child audits.
- **SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP** — cascade children of an audit-approved parent to `completed`/`done`.
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — release-ready parent must override/absorb `needsProducerReview` on children.
- **SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS** — test isolation: unit suite must never mutate the live worklog.
- **SA-0MSAL2NQV0008HY5** — audit runner stuck `in_progress` broke the release close step.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** added verification issues one `wl show` per attempted close (plus one per retry) — bounded by the candidate count; acceptable overhead for a release-time step.
- **Risk:** if the race also swallows the retry, the item is still reported unclosed — this is the intended visibility, not a regression.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "fix it in `wl` so closes never get lost" must be resisted here; record it as linked work on the ContextHub item rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** `getItemLifecycle` reflects the persisted state immediately after a successful `wl close` completes (no eventual-consistency delay beyond process exit).
- **Assumption:** `stage: done` is the terminal stage and `status: completed` the terminal status for a closed item.
- **Failure mode:** a `wl show` timeout/throw makes the item unverifiable → treated as unclosed (fail-safe), so the release never over-reports.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (the refiled ToneForge v0.1.2 race report plus the existing detailed work-item description) specified the failure, the required behaviour, and the acceptance criteria. Context was verified by repository inspection (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `run-release.js`, the injected `getItemLifecycleFn` boundary, and `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs`).

- Q: (not asked) Is `getItemLifecycle` an adequate verification boundary, or is a dedicated one needed? — Resolution: reuse `getItemLifecycleFn` where possible, or add a dedicated injectable `getCloseStateFn` defaulting to `getItemLifecycle`; either satisfies AC1. Source: repository inspection of `run-release.js` / `check-final-validation.js`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSRWB5LM0057VQ9** – [test-failure] closes work items ONLY after the merge is verified — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZEDED005YYIJ** – Docs: Update agent/ship.md & release docs (completed)
- **SA-0MUYADP50005EYA2** – Plan skill report shows 'incomplete' — pass planning-phase ACs, not feature ACs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, attempt, attempted (+138 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mujkpdaa002vvdp, acceptance, actually, add, attempt (+130 more)

# Migrate test-churn / TDD-value analysis to SorraAgents and make reporting reproducible

## Problem statement

The test-churn / TDD-value analysis capability currently lives in the ContextHub
repo as ad-hoc scripts (`scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` and its generated
artefacts). It hardcodes the ContextHub path, produces several incorrect metrics,
and is neither reusable nor tested as a skill. SorraAgents is the canonical home
for pi agent infrastructure, so the capability should be re-homed here and turned
into a first-class, reproducible skill that any project can invoke with one
command.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the pi agent infrastructure** — wants the capability owned by
  the canonical repo (`skill/`), documented, installed and tested like every
  other skill.
- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants reproducible TDD-ROI and test-growth
  evidence per project so conclusions are comparable over time.
- **Agent implementing testing-policy work** — wants a deterministic entry point
  (project root in, report + JSON out) that needs no code changes per repo.

Example user stories:

- As the maintainer, I want the analysis re-homed under `skill/test-churn/` and
  removed from ContextHub, so there is a single canonical implementation.
- As a producer, I want to run one command against any project root and get a
  self-contained `test_churn_report.md` plus `test_churn_data.json`, so results
  are reproducible and comparable.
- As an agent, I want the metrics corrected (real git status, honest rewrite
  ratios, distinct-commit rates, whole-file deletions) so policy decisions do
  not rest on wrong numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All analysis code, data and documentation are re-homed under a skill directory
   in SorraAgents and removed from ContextHub.
2. A reproducible skill (SKILL.md + scripts + tests) exists and can be invoked
   against any project root without code changes.
3. The skill computes the corrected metrics: real git name-status, documented
   rewrite-ratio denominators, distinct-commit temporal trend, and whole-file
   deletion accounting.
4. ContextHub work items `WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ` and `WL-0MV274I3R009XVZR` are
   re-homed or superseded, with provenance (IDs and commit hashes) recorded in
   both worklogs.
5. The skill is wired into `scripts/install_pi.sh` and covered by tests that pass.
6. Docs are updated and the change is pushed to `dev`.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must follow the repository skill contract (SKILL.md frontmatter: `name`,
  `description`; clear purpose, when-to-use, workflow, outputs).
- Skill scripts must resolve shared libraries from the canonical global skills
  location (`$(skill_path <name>)`) — never copy skill scripts between repos.
- No ContextHub-specific paths, files or conventions may remain in the skill;
  the project root must be a configurable argument.
- Work item descriptions and comments are written in Markdown and UK English.
- Cross-worklog migration is manual (`wl` stores are per-repo); relationships
  are recorded in descriptions/comments, not cross-store dependency edges.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is owned by the ship skill's release pipeline and is not
  hand-edited as part of this work.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` must install/symlink the new skill and expose it on a
  fresh install.

## Existing state

- ContextHub commit `141ceb8b` contains `scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`,
  `scripts/test_churn_data.json` and `scripts/TEST_CHURN_REPORT.md`; these
  artefacts still exist in the ContextHub checkout at `HEAD`.
- Known defects in the ContextHub script: hardcoded project path; file status
  hardcoded to `M` (new tests/deletions invisible); rewrite-ratio denominator
  excludes pure-addition modifications; temporal rate counts rewrite events, not
  distinct commits (can exceed 100%); `domain_churn` double-counts source files.
- ContextHub work items: `WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ` (source analysis) and
  `WL-0MV274I3R009XVZR` (accuracy defects, already deleted from ContextHub).
- SorraAgents already has the `skill/` tree, `scripts/install_pi.sh`,
  `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, and the curated
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` test anti-pattern guidance.

## Desired change

- Add `skill/test-churn/` containing a `SKILL.md`, the corrected analyser script
  (project root as argument), and its tests.
- Provide a deterministic entry point that emits `test_churn_report.md`
  (self-contained: scope, definitions, limitations, TDD-value assessment) and
  `test_churn_data.json` (machine-readable).
- Wire the skill into `scripts/install_pi.sh` and confirm a fresh install exposes
  it.
- Remove the analysis script/data/report from ContextHub.
- Record provenance for the ContextHub work items in both worklogs and document
  the migration in SorraAgents docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — New skill contract (frontmatter, purpose,
  workflow, outputs).
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — Ported analyser with
  project-root argument and corrected metrics.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_data.json` — Machine-readable analysis
  output (generated).
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_report.md` — Human-readable,
  self-contained report (generated).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_churn_analysis.py` — Unit tests for status
  classification, rewrite-ratio arithmetic, temporal aggregation and deletion
  accounting.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_skill_entrypoint.py` — End-to-end test on a small
  fixture repository.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — Install/symlink the new skill.
- `docs/dev/` — Documentation of the skill and the migration.

## Children

- Port test-churn analysis tooling and data to SorraAgents (`SA-0MV28WROY007NAB4`)
- Create the reproducible test-churn reporting skill (`SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS`)
- Re-home the ContextHub test-churn work items into SorraAgents (`SA-0MV28WSLP000WOJ8`)
  - Fix test churn analysis status detection and rewrite-ratio denominator (`SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW`)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope creep** — follow-on ideas discovered during the ContextHub analysis
  (scheduled runs `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU`, tests-deleted-vs-added metric
  `SA-0MV28WXPA003EHJC`, `toHaveBeenCalledWith` guidance `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`,
  mutation testing `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`) are tracked separately and must **not**
  be pulled into this epic.
- **Overlap** — the port child `SA-0MV28WROY007NAB4` AC3 already fixes the defects
  enumerated by `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW`; the two must be implemented together to
  avoid duplicated/conflicting changes.
- **Corrected figures** — fixing the metrics may change earlier ContextHub
  conclusions; the report must state corrected figures and flag any superseded
  numbers in the ContextHub report.
- **Performance** — scanning large git histories can be slow; the tool must be
  bounded and document its scope/limitations.
- **Assumption** — the ContextHub repo remains available for the source port
  (verified: artefacts present at `HEAD`).
- **Assumption** — `install_pi.sh` exposes any skill placed under `skill/`;
  verify on a fresh install rather than assuming.
- **Assumption** — no producer interview was required because the seed context
  and the four auto-completed children fully define the work.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ` — source test-churn analysis (to be
  superseded).
- ContextHub `WL-0MV274I3R009XVZR` — accuracy defects (re-homed as
  `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW`).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — existing anti-pattern guidance to
  align the skill's TDD-value conclusions with.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU`, `SA-0MV28WXPA003EHJC`, `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`,
  `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — blocked/follow-on items that depend on this epic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (epic description,
  four children with explicit ACs, and the ContextHub defect record) was
  sufficient to draft this brief. Research: inspected ContextHub artefacts at
  `HEAD` (`scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`, `scripts/test_churn_data.json`,
  `scripts/TEST_CHURN_REPORT.md`), SorraAgents `skill/` tree and
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`; searched the SorraAgents worklog for `test-churn`.
- **Decision (agent, Map):** children `SA-0MV28WROY007NAB4`,
  `SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS`, `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` and `SA-0MV28WSLP000WOJ8` were
  auto-completed to `intake_complete` (well-defined: clear headline, explicit
  measurable ACs, concise implementation notes). Source: `wl show --json`.
- **Open question (non-blocking):** the re-home child `SA-0MV28WSLP000WOJ8` AC5
  mentions updating the `CHANGELOG`; this epic treats `CHANGELOG.md` as owned by
  the ship release pipeline (per the skill contract). Assumption: the CHANGELOG
  entry is produced by the release process rather than hand-edited.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs introduced by StatusLifecycle migration (500d3f8) (completed)
- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** – [test-failure] test_audit_skill_doc.py::TestAuditSkillWorkItemIdDetection::test_scan_match_branch_structure — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15** – Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic (full cwd independence) (completed)

# Add a tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test-churn analysis to report test deletions as well as additions, and to support pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, so the suite does not grow without bound.

## Background

The ContextHub analysis found the suite grows roughly 8:1 (82,381 added vs 9,968 deleted lines in modified test files) and is ~2.17x the production source by code lines. The current tool's `--diff-filter=ADMR` also hides whole-file test deletions entirely, so pruning is invisible to the metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The analysis reports, per project and per test area: tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, and net growth, in the human report and JSON.
2. Whole-file test deletions are counted (diff filter includes D; rename detection applied so moves are not miscounted as deletions).
3. A documented review workflow describes how to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
4. The growth metric is trended over time (per quarter or per release) so regressions are visible.
5. Tests cover the added/deleted accounting, including files deleted and re-added.
6. The metric is exposed by the reproducible skill (see the migration epic) rather than as a standalone script.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (metric implemented there).

# Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Goal

As a producer, I want an empirical measure of whether the largest test suites actually detect faults, so conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on evidence rather than churn proxies.

## Background

Churn and line-count metrics cannot tell us whether tests earn their keep. The top-churn / largest suites identified by the ContextHub analysis (e.g. `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `sync.test.ts`, `database.test.ts`) are mock-heavy; mutation testing directly measures whether they detect injected faults. This is the recommended follow-up before firm TDD-ROI conclusions in WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented (e.g. Stryker for TypeScript, mutmut for Python), with rationale and licensing.
2. The tool runs against at least the top three churn modules of a target project and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
3. Results are compared with test size/mock density to test the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites have lower mutation scores.
4. Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment, with explicit caveats (sampling, runtime cost, equivalent mutants).
5. The campaign is reproducible (pinned tool version, documented command) and does not regress the project test suite.
6. Runtime cost is measured and bounded so the campaign can be run periodically.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (provides top-churn input).

# Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test-churn / test-health skill to run automatically on a schedule across all local projects, so test-suite growth and rewrite trends are monitored continuously without manual effort.

## Background

SorraAgents already supports scheduled prompts via `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (entries with `id`, `prompt`, `intervalDays`, optional `time`, `lastTriggeredAt`), used by e.g. `/skill:refactor` and `/skill:standup`. The new test-churn skill should be registered the same way for each project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduled entry is added for the test-churn/test-health skill in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (or the project-appropriate scheduled-prompts file) using the existing schema.
2. The schedule runs for every managed project, either via per-project entries or a single command that iterates configured project roots.
3. Output is written to a predictable location (e.g. `reports/test-churn/<date>.md`) and is idempotent (a re-run does not create duplicates).
4. Failures are surfaced (non-zero exit / logged) and do not silently pass.
5. The schedule interval is configurable and documented; the default is documented with a rationale.
6. Tests cover the scheduled-entry wiring or the iteration/adapter used to fan out across projects.
7. The setup is documented in the skill's SKILL.md and in the SorraAgents README/docs.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (the skill must exist first).

This work item was **re-homed from ContextHub** (origin: `WL-0MV274I3R009XVZR`) per producer

so the analysis code has **not yet been ported**. The fix must be applied to the
tooling once ported (or during porting), not in ContextHub.

---

# Fix test churn analysis status detection and rewrite-ratio denominator

## Defects found in scripts/test_churn_analysis.py (delivered by WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ)

### Defect 1 - File status is hardcoded to M
get_commit_diffs builds every FileChange with status=M and never consults git name-status. Consequences: commits_with_new_tests reported as 0 (actual 340, 20.4%); new_files always 0; analyse_test_first_signal status=A branches never fire, so the 86.0% test-first figure is invalid (it is co-evolution).

### Defect 2 - Rewrite-ratio denominator excludes pure-addition modifications
Correct denominators: deletions/(deletions+additions) over modified test files = 9968/92349 = 10.8%; including new test-file additions (232026) = 3.1%. Reported 21.1% overstates.

### Defect 3 - Temporal rate can exceed 100 percent
feature_commits_with_rewrites counts rewrite events not distinct commits; 2026-05 = 108.6% is not a commit percentage.

### Defect 4 - domain_churn double counts source files
adds len(src files) once per file in commit, inflating counts (section 11 unreliable).

## Acceptance criteria
1. Status detection uses real git name-status (A/M/D/R/T) with a test asserting A vs M.
2. Rewrite ratio computed with documented denominators; report modified-only and including-new-files variants.
3. Temporal rate counts distinct commits with at least one rewrite event.
4. domain_churn counts each file once.
5. Re-run and correct scripts/TEST_CHURN_REPORT.md and scripts/test_churn_data.json.
6. Unit tests cover each fixed function.

## Impact
Corrects AC1/AC2/AC3 evidence on the parent. Qualitative conclusion (tests mostly grow rather than get rewritten) stands; the 21.1% and 86% figures are wrong.
---
